newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: CenTra told to divest Chandler holdings.
newsitem.headline: CenTra told to divest Chandler holdings.

text.p: Chandler Insurance Co Ltd said the U.S. District Court for the District of Nebraska on March 25 ordered CenTra Inc and certain of its affiliates to divest themselves of all Chandler shares owned by them.
The CenTra defendants own or control 3,131,825 Chandler shares, representing about 45 percent of the outstanding stock, Chandler said late Wednesday.

The Court ordered Chandler's underwriting subsidiary, National American Insurance Co (NAICO), the CenTra defendants and the Nebraska Insurance Department to submit proposals to the Court by April 21, 1997, for the "orderly divestiture and dispositions" of the stock, Chandler said.
A hearing will then be scheduled to consider the proposals, Chandler said.

Chandler said it and NAICO are considering several alternatives but have not developed a final proposal at this time. Chandler shares closed Wednesday at 5-3/8 and were halted Thursday morning for news.

On March 27, 1997, the Court declined to exercise jurisdiction over 550,329 shares of Chandler stock held as security by Chandler subsidiaries for debts owed by two former NAICO agents but in which CenTra claimed to have option rights, Chandler said.
The Court's ruling clears the way for the subsidiaries to begin the process of disposing of these shares to retire the agents' debt, Chandler said.
Chandler also said a U.S. District Court jury in Oklahoma City, Okla., on April 9 returned verdicts in a lawsuit involving Chandler and CenTra.
The jury found in favor of CenTra and Amnex Inc on certain claims relating to their purchases of stock.
That resulted in awards against Chandler and an affiliate, Chandler Insurance (Barbados) Ltd, totaling $11,981,633, for which certain stock purchased by CenTra must be returned to the company.

Judge Vicki Miles LaGrange on April 1 dismissed CenTra's claims against NAICO and others for alleged wrongful cancellation in 1992 of CenTra's insurance policies with NAICO and an affiliate, NAICO Indemnity (Cayman) Ltd.

The jury also found in favor of plaintiffs and against certain officers or directors of Chandler on various claims, including securities and fiduciary duty claims, and awarded damages of $1 against each defendant.
Certain officers were also directed to repay bonuses received totaling $711,629, as well as a total of $25,000 for personal use of corporate aircraft, Chandler said.

CenTra's stock purchase and securities claims alleged that Chandler made inadequate disclosures about the applicability of the Nebraska Insurance Holding Company Systems Act to persons who purchase 10 percent or more of the company's stock, by virture of Chandler's parent relationship with NAICO, which is incorporated in Nebraska.
On other claims asserted by the CenTra Group, the jury found in favor of the company and individual defendants.
The jury also found in favor of NAICO and NAICO Indemnity on their counterclaims against CenTra for failure to pay insurance premiums in the sum of $788,625, Chandler said.

It also upheld a resolution adopted by the Chandler Board in August 1992, preventing CenTra and its affiliates from voting their Chandler stock as a result of purchases made by the CenTra Group in July, 1992 in its efforts to acquire control of Chandler, Chandler said.
In October, 1992, the Nebraska Insurance Department held that CenTra's attempt to take control of Chandler was in violation of Nebraska law and a threat to the interests of NAICO policyholders.
No verdicts were rendered by the jury against NAICO.
